title: Wave Superposition Beats Simulator
description: Three stacked plots of two sine waves and their sum on a shared time axis, with constructive/destructive shading and a derived beat envelope when the frequencies differ.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Acoustics
Signals and Systems

learningObjectives: Examine the summed waveform of two sine waves
Compare constructive and destructive interference regions
Relate the beat frequency to the difference of the two frequencies
prerequisites: A sine wave has frequency, amplitude, and phase

assumptions: Both waves have equal unit amplitude
A fixed 100 ms window is displayed at all frequency settings
limitations: Only two components; real interference involves many, and unequal amplitudes never cancel completely

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Three synchronized views for direct input-versus-result comparison
keyQuestions: What changes about the inputs when the sum cancels?
How many beats appear in 100 ms at a 20 Hz difference?
commonMisconceptions: That destructive interference makes the input waves smaller
That beats are a third tone rather than an amplitude variation
assessmentOpportunities: Infer a frequency difference from a heard beat rate
